title: Predicting expression-altering promoter mutations with deep learning

nodes.text: PromoterAI is a convolutional deep neural network that uses ~20 kb of sequence context around a promoter variant to predict its consequence on gene expression.
nodes.evidence: We introduce PromoterAI, a convolutional deep neural network model that uses ~20 kb of sequence context around a promoter variant to predict its expression consequence.

nodes.text: The model was first trained to predict histone modifications, DNA accessibility, transcription factor occupancy, and strand-specific CAGE at base-pair resolution around TSS, then fine-tuned on curated rare non-coding promoter variants associated with outlier expression.
nodes.evidence: We first trained the model to predict histone modifications, DNA accessibility, transcription factor (TF) occupancy, and strand-specific CAGE ... We subsequently fine-tuned the model using a curated set of rare non-coding promoter variants

nodes.text: Multi-tissue expression outliers for fine-tuning were derived from GTEx v8 by t-tests on expression z-scores after correcting for expression/genotype principal components, cis-eQTL effects, and trans-expression effects.
nodes.evidence: we subtracted out the contribution of other factors ... principal components ... cis-effects of common expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) ... and trans-effects of correlated patterns of gene expression

nodes.text: PromoterAI outperformed Evo2, DeepSEA, Basenji, ExPecto, Enformer, PuffinD, ChromBPNet, and Borzoi across three variant classification tasks, achieving auROC of 0.89 (under- vs over-expression), 0.80 (under-expression vs null), and 0.74 (over-expression vs null).
nodes.evidence: PromoterAI performed the best out of these models across all three metrics by achieving an auROC of 0.89, 0.80, and 0.74, respectively.

nodes.text: PromoterAI outperformed competing deep learning models on multiple MPRA saturation mutagenesis datasets, including the CAGI5 dataset of disease-associated gene promoters.
nodes.evidence: PromoterAI achieved the best performance (Fig. 1G, right, and fig. S1E)

nodes.text: PromoterAI's outlier-detection approach achieved greater enrichment of multi-tissue outliers than OUTRIDER's autoencoder and GTEx summary statistics (median z-scores and ANEVA-DOT) at matched false discovery rates.
nodes.evidence: Compared to the other methods, when choosing thresholds that result in the same false discovery rate in shuffled controls, our approach detected greater enrichment of multi-tissue outliers

nodes.text: Under-expression variants were enriched for disrupting ETS, YY1, ATF1, and NRF1 motifs, while overexpression outliers were enriched for disrupting E2F, NFKB, INSM1, ERR-alpha, and TFAP2 motifs.
nodes.evidence: Under-expression variants were particularly enriched for disrupting ETS motifs ... overexpression outliers were enriched for disrupting E2F motifs

nodes.text: It is generally easier for new variants to cause outlier expression by disrupting existing regulatory components than by creating new ones, highlighting the role of transcriptional repressors in promoter regulation.
nodes.evidence: it is generally easier for newly occurring variants to cause outlier gene expression by disrupting existing regulatory components rather than creating new ones

nodes.text: Fine-tuning with expression outliers overcame a limitation, highlighted in recent work, of predicting the directionality of motif effects, with the largest score changes falling at highly conserved positions despite conservation not being used in training.
nodes.evidence: fine-tuning may overcome limitations in predicting the directionality of motifs which has been highlighted in recent papers

nodes.text: Variants predicted to alter expression were strongly depleted of common relative to rare variants, indicating active negative selection; scores near +-0.5 approached missense-variant depletion and scores near +-1 approached nonsense-variant depletion.
nodes.evidence: At PromoterAI scores near +0.5 or -0.5, the observed depletion approached that of missense variants, while scores closer to +1 or -1 resulted in a depletion percentage comparable to that of nonsense variants.

nodes.text: Expression-altering variants showed greater depletion in promoters of high-pLI (constrained, dosage-sensitive) genes, and the depletion signal peaked within 100 bp of the TSS with under-expression variants being more deleterious.
nodes.evidence: We observed a greater depletion for expression-altering variants in the promoters of high pLI genes ... a notably stronger signal for under-expression than overexpression variants

nodes.text: Promoter variation is estimated to account for 6% of the genetic burden associated with rare diseases.
nodes.evidence: Our estimates suggest that promoter variation accounts for 6% of the genetic burden associated with rare diseases.

nodes.text: Canonical protein-coding promoter embeddings clustered into three classes: ubiquitously expressed (9,234 genes), bivalent chromatin (3,430 genes), and tissue-specific enhancer-like (6,632 genes), the latter resembling distal enhancer embeddings.
nodes.evidence: a first class of 9,234 genes ... a second class of 3,430 genes characterized by bivalent chromatin ... a third class of 6,632 genes with mainly tissue-specific expression
